To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Urgent: check your Brightline 6% developer – batch LX2291

Hi everyone,

Please check your Brightline developer before using it on anyone. Kelvin Trade has confirmed a filling error: some bottles labelled Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L, batch LX2291, may actually contain 12% (40 vol).

Stop using any bottle from this batch straight away. Kelvin says it was supplied between 19 October and 5 November, but please check the batch rather than relying on when you bought it.

The code is on the BASE OF THE BOTTLE, not the box. Check every bottle individually, including the open ones in your trolley as well as any stock in the back. If you’ve decanted any and can’t tell which bottle it came from, don’t use it until you can identify it.

This has already caused a scalp burn here. On Saturday I used a newly opened bottle from this batch for a bleach retouch. The lift was much faster than normal and my client’s scalp started burning; I rinsed straight away but she was left with red, sore patches. Aileen also checked hers after a highlights service on Thursday where the foils got very hot and the hair lifted much faster than expected. Hers was LX2291 too.

A stronger developer can make the hair lift too quickly and unevenly, leaving it patchy or brassy and potentially damaged. Heat, stinging or burning during a service needs attention straight away – please don’t assume it’s just the heater or normal tingling.

If someone reacts in the chair and you suspect a chemical burn:

- Stop the service immediately. Protect yourself with gloves and carefully remove any contaminated clothing if possible.
- Call 999 for medical help straight away. Don’t wait for blistering or severe pain. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also need an immediate 999 call.
- Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about an hour, following the call handler’s instructions. Don’t use shampoo, creams or other chemicals.
- Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Record what happened in the incident book at the desk.

The salon’s first aid reference is here: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/acid-and-chemical-burns/

Kelvin says affected bottles can be returned for full credit, either to the rep or to the Hillington depot. The rep is in Tuesday. If you’ve had a problem with a bottle, though, keep it back – don’t bin it or hand it over yet. Keep your notes, any dated photos and the supplier email too, and speak to your insurer about what they need.

Please pass this on to anyone else who buys from the Kelvin rep, and check your bottles before your next colour or bleach service.

reasons: The line telling people to keep dated photos, notes and the supplier email and to speak to their insurer comes from the private insurance note (d05) and hints at it.
